instructions: Core the 5 tomatoes and cut them into thin slices.
Peel the potatoes and cut them into slices about 1/4 inch thick. Cut the eggplant and the 2 zucchini into rounds about 1/2 inch thick.
Thinly slice the onion, finely chop the 2 garlic cloves and chop 1/4 cup of the parsley.
Lay half the tomato slices over the bottom of a large baking dish, about 9 by 13 inches or a little bigger. Sprinkle them with 1/2 tsp of the salt.
Spread the potatoes, eggplant and zucchini over the tomatoes in an even layer. Sprinkle on 1 tsp of the salt, 1/4 tsp of the pepper and the 1 tsp oregano.

Scatter the onion and garlic over the vegetables and lay the rest of the tomato slices on top. Sprinkle on the last 1/2 tsp salt and the last 1/4 tsp pepper, then the parsley. Drizzle the 2/3 cup olive oil evenly over everything.
Cover the dish tightly with foil and bake for 45 minutes.

Take off the foil and turn the vegetables gently with a spatula so the oily tomato coats everything. Bake uncovered for 45 minutes to 1 hour, until a knife slides easily into the potatoes and the top is browned in spots.
Let it sit for 10 minutes. Taste a piece of potato, and sprinkle on a pinch more salt if it's flat.
Serve warm or at room temperature with the feta and crusty bread.
method_notes: All three bake sliced potatoes and zucchini slowly with tomato, onion, garlic, parsley and a lot of olive oil until soft and browned. My Greek Dish layers sliced tomato under and over the potatoes, eggplant and zucchini, bakes it covered at 400°F, uncovers it halfway to toss and colour the top, and serves it with feta and bread. Souvlaki for the Soul skips the eggplant, tosses everything together with grated tomato in a single layer and bakes it uncovered at 350°F, and Diane Kochilas on SBS adds bell peppers and oregano and salts the zucchini first. This one follows My Greek Dish for 4, with the dried oregano its author suggests.
